 SPL 2026/27 Matchweek 7: Geylang and Sailors lock horns in clash of the week
 20 November, 2026 
 The 2026/27 Singapore Premier League (SPL) season resumes this weekend following the November international break, with a top-of-the-table clash between Geylang International and Lion City Sailors headlining the action. Elsewhere, unbeaten Tampines Rovers take on bottom-placed Hougang United, FC Jurong face Balestier Khalsa, while Young Lions, buoyed by their first win of the season, go up against Tanjong Pagar United.
 Jurong and Balestier eye return to winning ways 
 Fourth-placed FC Jurong and fifth-placed Balestier Khalsa are level on points in the SPL standings and go head-to-head in a Friday night clash at Jurong East, with both sides eager to get back on track.
 Jurong snapped a three-match losing streak in the SPL with a 1-1 draw against Tanjong Pagar United, while Balestier suffered a heavy 4-0 defeat to reigning champions Lion City Sailors in their last outing. Jurong last tasted victory in the SPL against Hougang United on September 18, securing a 3-0 win, while Balestier’s most recent success came against Young Lions on October 24 in a 2-1 victory.
 With both Jurong and Balestier having recorded two wins apiece so far, victory here would be crucial for either side as they look to avoid losing sight of the leading pack of Geylang International, the Sailors and Tampines Rovers.
 The Tigers claimed a 2-1 win when the two sides last met in April last season, and the White Swans will be keen to set the record straight. Jurong will be without Shunsuke Ono after the defender was sent off in their previous match against Tanjong Pagar, while Balestier welcome the return of defender Bill Mamadou in the squad selection following his four-match suspension.
 FC Jurong vs Balestier Khalsa | Friday, 20 November | 7:30pm | Jurong East Stadium | Watch on YouTube or meWATCH
 Young Lions aim to make it back-to-back wins 
 With their first win of the season behind them, Young Lions welcome Tanjong Pagar United to their home ground, Jalan Besar Stadium, on Saturday night as they look to build on that momentum.
 Firdaus Kassim’s side got off the mark in the 2026/27 SPL campaign with a 2-0 victory over Hougang United in their last outing, ending a 10-match winless run. Japanese midfielder Hisatoshi Nishido was the star of the show, scoring both goals to take his tally to three for the season. He will once again be central to the Young Lions’ hopes of building on that result.
 However, Young Lions will be without midfielder Garv Sahoo, who has been ruled out for the foreseeable future after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury while representing the Singapore Under-23s at the recent Gia Lai VTV Cup 2026 in Vietnam. Sahoo has been one of the team’s standout performers this season, contributing two assists.
 Tanjong Pagar head into the encounter without a win in their last two league outings, having suffered a 6-0 defeat to the Sailors before playing out a 1-1 draw with Jurong. Sitting sixth in the standings with two wins so far, the Jaguars will look to Boris Kopitovic and Riku Fukashiro for attacking inspiration as they seek to turn their fortunes around.
 They will also be without midfielder Jared Gallagher, who is suspended for the match after picking up his fourth yellow card of the season against Jurong.
 With a win and a draw in their two meetings this year, Young Lions are unbeaten against Tanjong Pagar and will be keen to maintain their positive record against the Jaguars.
 Young Lions vs Tanjong Pagar United | Saturday, 21 November | 7:30pm | Jalan Besar Stadium | Watch on YouTube or meWATCH 
 Sailors and Geylang set for top-of-the-table showdown   
 The 2026/27 SPL title race takes an early turn this Sunday as league leaders Geylang International face second-placed Lion City Sailors in a highly anticipated clash at Jalan Besar. Separated by just one point, both sides remain unbeaten, although the Sailors have played a game less. Victory for Mark Jackson’s men would see them leapfrog the Eagles and move to the top of the standings.
 The Sailors arrive in strong form, having won their last five matches across all competitions and scoring 19 goals in the process. They have also been impressive in the ACL Two, recording three consecutive victories, including back-to-back wins over Australia’s Adelaide United, 2-0 away before following up with a 5-0 home win.
 The Sailors also boast the league’s most potent attack, with 20 goals in five matches. Antonio Mance and Matthias Phaeton have led the charge, scoring four league goals apiece.
 At the other end of the pitch, Geylang have been equally impressive, conceding just twice in six league matches. Noor Ali’s side have also scored 12 goals, with Yang Hyeonju leading their attack on four goals and Dejan Racic scoring three. The Eagles were held to a goalless draw by Tampines Rovers in their previous outing but remain unbeaten with four wins and two draws.
 Recent meetings have favoured the Sailors, who have won the last three league encounters, including a 3-0 victory in April. However, Geylang will draw confidence from their last win over the defending champions on 4 May 2025, when they came from two goals down to claim a 3-2 victory at Our Tampines Hub.
 Lion City Sailors vs Geylang International | Sunday, 22 November | 7:30pm | Jalan Besar Stadium | Watch on YouTube or meWATCH 
 Unbeaten Tampines face struggling Hougang 
 In the other game on Sunday evening, Tampines Rovers take on Hougang United at Bishan as they look to return to winning ways in the SPL.
 The Stags’ four-match winning run in the league ended with a goalless draw against Eastern rivals Geylang International in the Eastern Derby before the international break. However, Nazri Nasir’s men head into this clash on the back of a come-from-behind 3-2 win over Thailand’s Ratchaburi FC in the Shopee Cup on Wednesday night, securing their first victory in the competition.
 Hougang remain in search of their first win of the 2026/27 season and will have their work cut out against Tampines. The Cheetahs fell 2-0 to Young Lions in their last league outing, extending their losing streak to five matches and leaving them rooted to the bottom of the standings. Having scored just four goals in the league so far, the likes of Oakley Cannonier, Ayman Kassimi and Connor Flynn-Gillespie will need to offer greater firepower if Hougang are to start picking up points.
 Hougang’s Montenegrin defender Milos Drincic is also available for selection again after serving his suspension.
 Recent form favours the Stags, who have come out on top in each of their last five encounters with Hougang United. The Cheetahs have not beaten Tampines since their 4-2 victory on 25 January 2025.
